title: Giordano Bruno is burned at the stake in Rome
summary: The Roman Inquisition had the philosopher Giordano Bruno burned alive in the Campo de' Fiori after a trial lasting seven years.
reason: Bruno taught an infinite universe with many worlds and held views the Church judged heretical, and he refused to recant them.
significance: He became a lasting symbol of free thought persecuted by religious authority.

title: Huaynaputina erupts in Peru
summary: The volcano Huaynaputina in southern Peru began the largest eruption in recorded South American history, burying villages and spreading ash over Arequipa.
reason: Magma rising beneath the Andes, where the Nazca plate sinks under South America, built pressure until the volcano exploded.
significance: Its ash cooled the Northern Hemisphere and contributed to the famine of 1601 to 1603 in Russia.

title: Tokugawa Ieyasu wins the Battle of Sekigahara
summary: The eastern army of Tokugawa Ieyasu defeated the western coalition loyal to the Toyotomi clan at Sekigahara, helped by defections during the battle.
reason: After the death of Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1598, his regents split into rival camps competing for control of Japan.
significance: The victory gave Ieyasu control of Japan and led to two and a half centuries of Tokugawa rule.

title: Elizabeth I charters the East India Company
summary: Queen Elizabeth I granted a royal charter to a group of London merchants, giving them a monopoly on English trade east of the Cape of Good Hope.
reason: English merchants wanted a share of the lucrative spice trade dominated by the Portuguese and the Dutch.
significance: The company grew into a power that conquered and ruled much of India for Britain.

title: Dutch East India Company is founded
summary: The States General of the Netherlands chartered the United East India Company (VOC), merging rival trading firms into one company with a monopoly on Asian trade.
reason: Competing Dutch companies were driving down profits, and the Republic wanted a strong body to fight Portugal and Spain in Asia.
significance: Often called the first multinational corporation, it issued tradable shares and dominated Asian trade for nearly two centuries.

title: Tokugawa Ieyasu becomes shogun of Japan
summary: Emperor Go-Yozei appointed Tokugawa Ieyasu as shogun, founding the Tokugawa shogunate with its seat at Edo.
reason: Ieyasu's victory at Sekigahara made him the dominant warlord, and the title gave his rule legitimacy.
significance: The Tokugawa shogunate ruled a unified and largely peaceful Japan until 1868.

title: James VI of Scotland inherits the English throne
summary: Queen Elizabeth I died without children and James VI of Scotland succeeded her as James I of England, joining the two crowns under one monarch.
reason: James was the great-grandson of Henry VII and the closest Protestant heir to the childless queen.
significance: The personal union of England and Scotland laid the ground for the later United Kingdom.

title: Cervantes publishes the first part of Don Quixote
summary: The first part of Miguel de Cervantes' novel about a would-be knight and his squire Sancho Panza was published in Madrid.
reason: Cervantes satirized the popular chivalric romances of his time while portraying Spanish society with irony and warmth.
significance: It is widely considered the first modern novel and one of the most influential works of literature.

title: The Gunpowder Plot is foiled in London
summary: Guy Fawkes was arrested guarding barrels of gunpowder in a cellar beneath the House of Lords, ending a plot to blow up Parliament and King James I.
reason: A group of English Catholics led by Robert Catesby hoped to kill the Protestant king and restore a Catholic monarchy.
significance: Its failure is still marked each year on Bonfire Night and hardened anti-Catholic laws in England.
place: Palace of Westminster, London, United Kingdom

title: Willem Janszoon makes the first recorded European landing in Australia
summary: The Dutch ship Duyfken under Willem Janszoon landed at the Pennefather River on the Cape York Peninsula, the first documented European landing on Australia.
reason: The Dutch East India Company sent Janszoon from Banten to search for trade opportunities around New Guinea.
significance: It began European contact with the Australian continent.
place: Pennefather River, Cape York Peninsula, Australia

title: Monteverdi's L'Orfeo premieres in Mantua
summary: Claudio Monteverdi's opera L'Orfeo, telling the myth of Orpheus, was first performed at the ducal court of Mantua.
reason: The Gonzaga court sponsored the new art of sung drama that Florentine composers had begun a few years earlier.
significance: It is the earliest opera still regularly performed and set the model for the form.

title: English colonists found Jamestown in Virginia
summary: About one hundred settlers sent by the Virginia Company landed on a peninsula of the James River and founded the fort of Jamestown.
reason: The company hoped to profit from gold, trade and land in North America and to rival Spain's American empire.
significance: Jamestown became the first permanent English settlement in the Americas.

title: Samuel de Champlain founds Quebec
summary: The French explorer Samuel de Champlain built a fortified trading post at a narrowing of the Saint Lawrence River, the beginning of Quebec City.
reason: France wanted a permanent base for the fur trade and for its claims in North America.
significance: Quebec became the capital of New France and the heart of French-speaking Canada.

title: Hans Lipperhey applies for a patent on the telescope
summary: The spectacle maker Hans Lipperhey of Middelburg asked the States General in The Hague for a patent on a device that made distant things appear near.
reason: Lens makers had found that combining a convex and a concave lens magnified distant objects, and Lipperhey sought exclusive rights.
significance: It is the earliest written record of a telescope, which soon transformed astronomy.

title: Galileo discovers the moons of Jupiter
summary: Looking through his improved telescope in Padua, Galileo Galilei saw small points of light beside Jupiter, which over the following nights he identified as moons orbiting it.
reason: Galileo had built telescopes far stronger than the first Dutch models and turned them systematically to the sky.
significance: Bodies orbiting another planet undermined the Earth-centered model and supported Copernicus.

title: Michael Romanov is elected tsar of Russia
summary: An assembly of the land in Moscow chose the young Michael Romanov as tsar, ending the Time of Troubles.
reason: Years of famine, civil war and Polish and Swedish invasion after the end of the Rurik dynasty left Russia without a ruler.
significance: It founded the Romanov dynasty, which ruled Russia until 1917.

title: Osaka Castle falls and the Toyotomi line ends
summary: Tokugawa forces stormed Osaka Castle at the end of the summer campaign, and Toyotomi Hideyori and his mother took their own lives as it burned.
reason: Hideyori remained a rallying point for opponents of the Tokugawa, and Ieyasu wanted to remove the last rival claim to power.
significance: It removed the final challenge to the Tokugawa shogunate.

title: Le Maire and Schouten round Cape Horn
summary: Dutch navigators Jacob Le Maire and Willem Schouten sailed past the southern tip of South America and named it Kaap Hoorn after the town of Hoorn.
reason: They sought a route to the Pacific outside the Strait of Magellan, which the Dutch East India Company's monopoly controlled.
significance: It opened the Cape Horn route that sailing ships used for three centuries.

title: Defenestration of Prague sparks the Bohemian Revolt
summary: Protestant Bohemian nobles threw two Catholic imperial governors and their secretary out of a window of Prague Castle; all three survived.
reason: The Protestant estates protested against Habsburg violations of their religious freedoms and the rule of the Catholic Ferdinand.
significance: The revolt that followed started the Thirty Years' War.

title: Jan Pieterszoon Coen captures Jayakarta and founds Batavia
summary: Dutch forces under Jan Pieterszoon Coen took the port of Jayakarta on Java, razed it and built Batavia on its site.
reason: The Dutch East India Company needed a fortified headquarters in Asia and wanted to control the trade routes of the archipelago.
significance: Batavia, today Jakarta, became the center of Dutch power in Asia for more than three centuries.

title: Catholic forces crush Bohemia at White Mountain
summary: Imperial and Catholic League armies routed the Bohemian Protestant army outside Prague within a few hours.
reason: Emperor Ferdinand II set out to end the Bohemian revolt and remove Frederick V, whom the rebels had elected king.
significance: Bohemia lost its independence and was forcibly re-Catholicized under Habsburg rule.

title: Pilgrims sign the Mayflower Compact
summary: Aboard the Mayflower off Cape Cod, 41 male passengers signed an agreement to form a civil body politic and obey its laws.
reason: The ship had landed outside the Virginia Company's territory, so the settlers needed their own basis of government to keep order.
significance: It became an early model of self-government by consent in America.

title: Pope Urban VIII consecrates the new St. Peter's Basilica
summary: After 120 years of building, the new basilica of St. Peter in Rome, with Michelangelo's dome, was consecrated by Pope Urban VIII.
reason: The old Constantinian basilica was crumbling, and the popes wanted a church to express the glory of Rome.
significance: It became the largest church of its age and the central symbol of the Catholic Church.

title: Death of Mumtaz Mahal inspires the Taj Mahal
summary: Mumtaz Mahal, the beloved wife of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, died in Burhanpur giving birth to her fourteenth child.
reason: She had accompanied her husband on a military campaign in the Deccan, and the birth went badly.
significance: Grieving, Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in Agra as her tomb.

title: Gustavus Adolphus is killed at the Battle of Lutzen
summary: Swedish forces defeated the imperial army of Albrecht von Wallenstein near Lutzen in Saxony, but King Gustavus Adolphus died in the fighting.
reason: Sweden had entered the Thirty Years' War to protect German Protestants and its own power on the Baltic.
significance: The loss of its king weakened the Protestant cause and prolonged the war.

title: Galileo is forced to recant heliocentrism
summary: The Roman Inquisition found Galileo vehemently suspect of heresy, and he formally abjured the view that the Earth moves around the Sun; he spent the rest of his life under house arrest.
reason: His Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems had defended Copernicus and offended Pope Urban VIII.
significance: The trial became the classic example of conflict between science and religious authority.
place: Santa Maria sopra Minerva, Rome, Italy

title: Joseon king submits to the Qing at Samjeondo
summary: King Injo of Joseon left his besieged fortress and bowed before Hong Taiji at Samjeondo, accepting the Qing as overlord of Korea.
reason: Hong Taiji invaded Korea to force it to break its loyalty to the Ming dynasty, his enemy.
significance: Korea became a tributary of the Qing, freeing the Manchus to concentrate on conquering China.

title: Shimabara Rebellion breaks out in Japan
summary: Peasants and masterless samurai, many of them Christians, rose against their lord on the Shimabara Peninsula in Kyushu.
reason: Crushing taxes during famine and the persecution of Japanese Christians drove the population to revolt.
significance: Its suppression led the shogunate to expel the Portuguese and seal Japan off from most foreign contact.

title: Ottomans recapture Baghdad from Safavid Persia
summary: After a siege led personally by Sultan Murad IV, the Safavid garrison of Baghdad surrendered and the city returned to Ottoman rule.
reason: Persia had taken Baghdad in 1624, and Murad IV was determined to restore Ottoman control of Mesopotamia.
significance: It settled Iraq in Ottoman hands until the First World War.

title: Ottomans and Safavids sign the Treaty of Zuhab
summary: The Ottoman Empire and Safavid Persia made peace, dividing the Caucasus and leaving Mesopotamia to the Ottomans.
reason: More than a century of wars between the two empires had exhausted both after the Ottoman recapture of Baghdad.
significance: Its frontier roughly matches today's border between Iran and its western neighbours Turkey and Iraq.

title: The Dutch capture Malacca from the Portuguese
summary: After a siege of several months with help from the Sultanate of Johor, the Dutch East India Company forced the Portuguese garrison of Malacca to surrender.
reason: Control of Malacca meant control of the strait linking the Indian Ocean with the South China Sea.
significance: It ended Portuguese dominance in Southeast Asia and made the Dutch the leading European power there.

title: Abel Tasman sights Tasmania
summary: The Dutch navigator Abel Tasman sighted the west coast of an island he named Van Diemen's Land, now Tasmania.
reason: The Dutch East India Company sent him from Batavia to explore the unknown southern lands and possible routes to South America.
significance: It was the first European sighting of Tasmania, and weeks later Tasman also reached New Zealand.
place: West coast of Tasmania, near Macquarie Harbour, Australia

title: Beijing falls and the last Ming emperor hangs himself
summary: As Li Zicheng's rebel army entered Beijing, the Chongzhen Emperor hanged himself on a hill behind the Forbidden City.
reason: Famine, heavy taxes and decades of war against the Manchus had driven millions of peasants into rebellion.
significance: It ended Ming rule in Beijing and opened the way for the Qing conquest of China.

title: Qing and Wu Sangui defeat Li Zicheng at Shanhai Pass
summary: The Ming general Wu Sangui joined forces with the Manchu Qing army and defeated Li Zicheng's rebels at the eastern end of the Great Wall.
reason: Wu Sangui preferred alliance with the Manchus to submission to the rebel who had taken Beijing.
significance: The Qing entered China through the pass, took Beijing and ruled China until 1912.

title: Peace of Westphalia ends the Thirty Years' War
summary: Treaties signed at Munster and Osnabruck ended the Thirty Years' War in the Holy Roman Empire and the Eighty Years' War between Spain and the Dutch.
reason: Three decades of war had devastated Central Europe and exhausted all sides without a decisive victory.
significance: It established principles of state sovereignty that shaped the modern international order.

title: King Charles I of England is executed
summary: After being convicted of treason by a special court of Parliament, Charles I was beheaded outside the Banqueting House in Whitehall.
reason: Charles had lost two civil wars against Parliament and was blamed for renewing the bloodshed by seeking Scottish help.
significance: England became a republic, and the public trial of a reigning king shook monarchies across Europe.
place: Banqueting House, Whitehall, London, United Kingdom

title: Jan van Riebeeck founds a Dutch station at the Cape
summary: Jan van Riebeeck arrived in Table Bay with three ships and set up a fort and garden to supply Dutch East India Company ships.
reason: Ships sailing between Europe and Asia needed fresh water, food and repairs halfway along the long voyage.
significance: The outpost grew into Cape Town and the start of European settlement in South Africa.
place: Table Bay, Cape Town, South Africa

title: Cossacks swear allegiance to the Tsar at Pereiaslav
summary: A Cossack council led by Hetman Bohdan Khmelnytsky agreed at Pereiaslav to place the Cossack Hetmanate under the protection of the Russian tsar.
reason: The Cossacks, in revolt against Poland-Lithuania since 1648, needed a strong ally to survive.
significance: It brought much of Ukraine under Russian rule and remains contested in Ukrainian and Russian memory.

title: Great Fire of Meireki destroys most of Edo
summary: A fire fanned by strong winds burned for three days in Edo, the shogun's capital, destroying most of the city and Edo Castle's main tower.
reason: Edo was densely built of wood and paper, and a long dry spell had left it vulnerable.
significance: About 100,000 people may have died, and the city was rebuilt with firebreaks and wider streets.

title: Koxinga forces the Dutch to surrender Taiwan
summary: After a nine-month siege, the Dutch governor Frederick Coyett signed the surrender of Fort Zeelandia to the Ming loyalist commander Koxinga.
reason: Koxinga, losing the war against the Qing on the mainland, needed a secure base and attacked the Dutch colony on Taiwan.
significance: It ended Dutch rule in Taiwan and began Chinese settlement of the island under the Kingdom of Tungning.

title: Great Fire of London breaks out
summary: A fire began in a bakery on Pudding Lane and spread for four days, destroying most of the medieval City of London, including St Paul's Cathedral.
reason: A long dry summer, strong east winds and tightly packed timber houses let the blaze spread faster than it could be stopped.
significance: The city was rebuilt in brick and stone, and the disaster led to modern fire insurance.

title: Shivaji is crowned Chhatrapati of the Maratha kingdom
summary: The Maratha leader Shivaji was crowned king with Vedic rites at the hill fort of Raigad, taking the title Chhatrapati.
reason: Shivaji had carved out an independent state against the Mughals and Bijapur and wanted formal royal standing.
significance: The Maratha state he founded later became the dominant power in India.

title: Leeuwenhoek reports seeing microorganisms
summary: In a letter to the Royal Society, the Delft draper Antonie van Leeuwenhoek described tiny living creatures he had seen in water through his own microscopes.
reason: Leeuwenhoek ground lenses of unmatched quality and was curious to examine everything from rainwater to pepper infusions.
significance: It was the first report of single-celled life and founded microbiology.

title: Pueblo Revolt drives the Spanish from New Mexico
summary: Pueblo peoples led by Popé rose together across New Mexico, killing hundreds of colonists and priests and forcing the Spanish to abandon Santa Fe.
reason: Spanish forced labor, drought, and the suppression of Pueblo religion had made colonial rule unbearable.
significance: It was one of the most successful Indigenous uprisings against European rule in North America.
place: Santa Fe, New Mexico, United States

title: La Salle claims the Mississippi basin for France
summary: Having descended the Mississippi to the Gulf of Mexico, Rene-Robert Cavelier de La Salle claimed the whole river basin for Louis XIV and named it Louisiana.
reason: France wanted to link its Canadian colony with the Gulf and block English and Spanish expansion in the interior.
significance: It gave France a claim to the heart of North America, later sold to the United States in 1803.
participants: Rene-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle
place: Mississippi River delta, Louisiana, United States

title: Louis XIV moves his court to Versailles
summary: King Louis XIV officially moved the royal court and government of France from Paris to the palace he had built at Versailles.
reason: Louis wanted to escape the unrest of Paris and keep the nobility close and dependent on royal favor.
significance: Versailles became the model of absolute monarchy and of court life across Europe.

title: Battle of Vienna breaks the Ottoman siege
summary: A relief army led by King John III Sobieski of Poland attacked from the Kahlenberg and routed the Ottoman army besieging Vienna.
reason: Grand Vizier Kara Mustafa Pasha had marched on the Habsburg capital to expand Ottoman power into Central Europe.
significance: It marked the end of Ottoman expansion in Europe and the start of their retreat from Hungary.

title: Louis XIV revokes the Edict of Nantes
summary: With the Edict of Fontainebleau, Louis XIV outlawed Protestantism in France, ordering churches destroyed and pastors expelled.
reason: The king sought religious unity under Catholicism as part of his absolute rule.
significance: Some 200,000 Huguenots fled to Protestant countries, taking their skills and businesses with them.

title: Newton publishes the Principia
summary: Isaac Newton's Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica was published in London, setting out the laws of motion and universal gravitation.
reason: Edmond Halley urged Newton to publish his work after asking him about the orbits of planets, and paid for the printing himself.
significance: It founded classical mechanics and became one of the most important works in the history of science.

title: William of Orange lands at Torbay
summary: William of Orange landed at Brixham in Devon with a Dutch army of about 15,000 men, and King James II soon fled to France.
reason: English nobles invited William to intervene after the birth of a Catholic heir to the Catholic King James II.
significance: The Glorious Revolution put Parliament above the crown and made England a constitutional monarchy.

title: The English Bill of Rights becomes law
summary: The Bill of Rights received royal assent, limiting the powers of the crown and guaranteeing rights of Parliament and of subjects.
reason: Parliament wanted to secure the gains of the Glorious Revolution and prevent a return to the arbitrary rule of James II.
significance: It shaped later constitutions, including the United States Bill of Rights.
place: Palace of Westminster, London, United Kingdom

title: William III defeats James II at the Boyne
summary: The army of William III crossed the River Boyne and defeated the forces of the deposed James II, who fled back to France.
reason: James had landed in Ireland with French help, hoping to use Catholic Ireland as a base to win back his crown.
significance: It secured Protestant rule in Ireland and is still commemorated by Ulster loyalists.

title: An earthquake sinks much of Port Royal, Jamaica
summary: A strong earthquake liquefied the sandy spit on which Port Royal stood, and much of the city slid into the sea, followed by a tsunami.
reason: Port Royal was built on loose sand and gravel, which turned to liquid when the ground shook.
significance: About 2,000 people died at once and the richest port of the English Caribbean was ruined.

title: The Bank of England is founded
summary: A royal charter created the Governor and Company of the Bank of England, which lent 1.2 million pounds to the government.
reason: King William III needed money to fight France, and investors were offered interest and banking privileges in return.
significance: It became the model for central banks and for modern public debt.

title: Omani forces take Fort Jesus from the Portuguese
summary: After a siege of nearly three years, Omani Arabs stormed Fort Jesus at Mombasa, the main Portuguese stronghold on the Swahili coast.
reason: The Sultanate of Oman sought to drive the Portuguese from East Africa and take over the Indian Ocean trade.
significance: It ended Portuguese power north of Mozambique and began Omani dominance on the East African coast.

title: Treaty of Karlowitz forces the first great Ottoman cession
summary: The Ottoman Empire signed peace with the Holy League at Karlowitz, giving up most of Hungary and Transylvania to the Habsburgs and other lands to Venice and Poland.
reason: Sixteen years of defeats after the failed siege of Vienna had left the Ottomans unable to continue.
significance: It was the first time the Ottomans ceded large territories to Europe, and Habsburg Austria became a great power.

title: Great Cascadia earthquake strikes the Pacific Northwest
summary: A magnitude 9 earthquake ruptured the Cascadia subduction zone off western North America and sent a tsunami across the Pacific to Japan.
reason: Strain built up for centuries as the Juan de Fuca plate slid beneath the North American plate, until the fault slipped all at once.
significance: Dated from Japanese tsunami records and drowned forests, it shows the threat of a future great quake in the region.
participants: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest
place: Cascadia subduction zone, off Oregon, United States

title: Charles XII routs the Russian army at Narva
summary: A small Swedish army under the 18-year-old Charles XII attacked in a snowstorm and destroyed a much larger Russian army besieging Narva.
reason: Russia, Denmark and Saxony had attacked Sweden to break its hold on the Baltic, starting the Great Northern War.
significance: The defeat pushed Peter the Great to modernize the Russian army.

title: Frederick I crowns himself King in Prussia
summary: Elector Frederick III of Brandenburg crowned himself Frederick I, King in Prussia, in Konigsberg.
reason: He won the emperor's consent by promising troops for the coming War of the Spanish Succession.
significance: The new Kingdom of Prussia grew into the power that later unified Germany.

title: Peter the Great founds Saint Petersburg
summary: Peter the Great laid the foundation of the Peter and Paul Fortress on an island in the Neva delta, the beginning of Saint Petersburg.
reason: Peter had just won the Neva mouth from Sweden and wanted a port and a new capital facing Europe.
significance: Saint Petersburg became the capital of Russia for two centuries and its window to the West.
place: Peter and Paul Fortress, Saint Petersburg, Russia

title: Marlborough and Eugene win the Battle of Blenheim
summary: An allied army under the Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy crushed a Franco-Bavarian army on the Danube.
reason: France and Bavaria were threatening Vienna, and its fall would have knocked Austria out of the War of the Spanish Succession.
significance: It saved Vienna and ended the reputation of French armies as invincible.

title: Death of Aurangzeb begins the Mughal decline
summary: The Mughal emperor Aurangzeb died at Ahmednagar in the Deccan, aged 88, after nearly fifty years on the throne.
reason: His long wars against the Marathas and his successors' struggles over the throne had drained the empire.
significance: The Mughal Empire fragmented soon after, opening India to regional powers and European companies.

title: England and Scotland unite as Great Britain
summary: The Acts of Union came into force, joining the kingdoms of England and Scotland into a single Kingdom of Great Britain with one parliament at Westminster.
reason: England wanted to secure the Protestant succession, and Scotland, hit by the failed Darien scheme, wanted access to English markets.
significance: It created the British state that became the center of a global empire.

title: Mount Fuji erupts for the last time
summary: Mount Fuji began the Hoei eruption, throwing out ash for two weeks that fell as far as Edo, about 100 kilometers away.
reason: The great Hoei earthquake seven weeks earlier is thought to have disturbed the magma chamber below the volcano.
significance: It is Fuji's most recent eruption and the reference case for planning against its next one.

title: Peter the Great crushes Sweden at Poltava
summary: The Russian army under Peter the Great destroyed the Swedish army of Charles XII near Poltava in Ukraine; the king fled to the Ottoman Empire.
reason: Charles had invaded Russia to end the Great Northern War, but winter and lost supplies weakened his army.
significance: It ended Sweden's era as a great power and made Russia the dominant power in Eastern Europe.

title: Peace of Utrecht ends the War of the Spanish Succession
summary: France signed treaties at Utrecht with Britain, the Dutch Republic and others, recognizing Philip V as king of Spain while barring the union of the French and Spanish crowns.
reason: More than a decade of war over the Spanish throne had exhausted the powers involved.
significance: Britain gained Gibraltar, Newfoundland and the slave trade asiento, beginning its rise to world power.

title: Louis XIV dies after a 72-year reign
summary: Louis XIV, the Sun King, died at Versailles of gangrene, leaving the throne to his five-year-old great-grandson Louis XV.
reason: His long reign had outlived his son and grandson, so the crown passed to a child under a regency.
significance: His reign, the longest of any European monarch, defined absolute monarchy, but left France deep in debt.

title: Treaty of Nystad ends the Great Northern War
summary: Sweden and Russia made peace at Nystad, ceding Livonia, Estonia, Ingria and part of Karelia to Russia.
reason: After two decades of war, Sweden had lost its army and its allies and could no longer resist Russian attacks on its coast.
significance: Russia gained its Baltic coastline and replaced Sweden as the leading power of Northern Europe.

title: Peter the Great is proclaimed Emperor of All Russia
summary: After the peace with Sweden, the Russian Senate gave Peter the titles Emperor of All Russia and Father of the Fatherland, turning the tsardom into the Russian Empire.
reason: Victory in the Great Northern War let Peter claim equal standing with the great empires of Europe.
significance: The Russian Empire lasted until 1917 and became one of the largest states in history.

title: Jacob Roggeveen reaches Easter Island
summary: The Dutch explorer Jacob Roggeveen sighted a remote Pacific island on Easter Sunday and named it Easter Island; his men landed and saw its great stone statues.
reason: Roggeveen was searching for the supposed southern continent on behalf of the Dutch West India Company.
significance: It was the first known European contact with Rapa Nui and its moai.

title: Bach's St Matthew Passion is first performed
summary: Johann Sebastian Bach's St Matthew Passion, for two choirs and two orchestras, was performed at the Good Friday vespers in Leipzig's St. Thomas Church.
reason: As cantor of St. Thomas, Bach had to supply music for the Lutheran liturgy, including a passion for Good Friday.
significance: It is one of the summits of Western sacred music.

title: Nader Shah is crowned king of Persia
summary: At a great assembly on the Mughan plain, the general Nader was proclaimed Shah of Iran, ending the Safavid dynasty.
reason: Nader had driven out the Afghans, Ottomans and Russians, and was already the real ruler behind a child Safavid shah.
significance: He founded the Afsharid dynasty and briefly made Persia the strongest power in Asia west of China.

title: Nader Shah defeats the Mughal army at Karnal
summary: The Persian army of Nader Shah routed a much larger Mughal army in a few hours near Karnal, north of Delhi.
reason: Nader invaded India to seize the riches of the declining Mughal Empire, using its sheltering of Afghan rebels as a pretext.
significance: Nader then sacked Delhi and took the Peacock Throne, exposing the weakness of the Mughals.

title: Massacre of the Chinese in Batavia
summary: Dutch soldiers and local residents killed thousands of ethnic Chinese in Batavia over several days in a massacre that began on 9 October.
reason: Unemployment among Chinese sugar workers, plans to deport them, and rumors of a Chinese uprising stirred panic among the colonial authorities.
significance: It was one of the worst atrocities of Dutch colonial rule and sparked the Java War against the company.

title: Handel's Messiah premieres in Dublin
summary: George Frideric Handel's oratorio Messiah was first performed at the Great Music Hall on Fishamble Street in Dublin, as a charity concert.
reason: Handel had been invited to Dublin for a season of concerts to raise money for local charities and prisoners.
significance: It became one of the most performed choral works in the world.

title: Earthquake and tsunami destroy Lima and Callao
summary: A great earthquake struck Lima, the capital of Spanish Peru, and a tsunami wiped out the nearby port of Callao, leaving only a few survivors there.
reason: Peru lies above the boundary where the Nazca plate dives under South America, a zone of frequent large earthquakes.
significance: It was one of the deadliest disasters in colonial South America and led to the rebuilding of Lima.

title: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle ends the War of the Austrian Succession
summary: Britain, France and the Dutch Republic signed peace at Aachen, later joined by the other powers, largely restoring conquests on both sides.
reason: Eight years of war over the succession of Maria Theresa had become costly for all sides without a clear winner.
significance: Prussia kept Silesia, and the unresolved rivalries led to the Seven Years' War.
